S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report any thermal event involving fire, uncontrolled overheating, evacuation, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a fuller incident report within 10 business days. Other confirmed thermal incidents must be reported within 10 business days. Manufacturers must notify affected customers promptly when an incident indicates a material safety risk, and no later than 5 business days after that risk is confirmed.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a standardized, independently witnessed sustained-heat test at 55 °C before sale and at least annually thereafter, using a representative sample and published protocol. Customers purchasing a model must receive that model’s per-model test results and any associated corrective actions before purchase; results must also be provided to existing owners when they indicate a material safety risk. A failure rate above 5% requires prompt regulator notification and a corrective-action plan. A rate above 8% requires suspension of new sales until the regulator accepts the plan and verifies effective corrective action.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New home battery units placed on the market must support secure remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized access and a locally accessible shut-off method. Manufacturers must provide a retrofit pathway for already-installed units and complete retrofits within 6 years of this standard taking effect. Where a retrofit is technically infeasible, the manufacturer must notify the owner and regulator, explain the limitation, and provide an equivalent risk-reduction measure.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery units placed on the market must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after this standard takes effect.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: Manufacturers must provide customers with clear safety notices for confirmed incidents or test results indicating a material risk, without undue delay and no later than 5 business days after confirming the risk. A manufacturer must notify the regulator and initiate a recall when any model’s annual thermal-incident rate exceeds 8 per 100,000 installed units, or sooner when the regulator determines that a material risk requires recall.

document.section_notes: S1 requires 24h serious reporting and 14d other reporting with customer notice within 7d, but only confirmed incidents. S2 sets a 55°C test, 5% corrective-action trigger and 8% sales suspension, with per-model results to purchasers but not public. S3 mandates new-unit shut-off immediately and retrofit within 6 years with feasibility escape. S4 requires built-in suppression at 36 months. S5 mandates recall above 8/100k with notices within 7d and no serious-injury clause.
